title: Joint tuning of KV quantization and expert residency - execution and acceptance
protocol: offload, num-tokens 32768, memory-ratio 0.90, 16k greedy decode + /v1/score PPL. A = same slots (cache 2600, isolates codec). B = same VRAM (--moe-cache-auto, captures residency).
analysis: Same slots isolates the codec: nvfp4 18.52 vs bf16 18.47 (equal) vs fp8 17.65 (-4.6%) -> the codec alone does not speed decode.

Same VRAM: fp8 24.45 vs nvfp4 23.68 vs bf16 23.82, all within ~3% (noise); fp8's B edge is NOT a residency gain (it resolved FEWER slots, 3915 < 3979) and A shows fp8 slower, so the B ordering is noise.
PPL vs bf16: fp8 +0.055%, nvfp4 +0.42% -> small; nvfp4 keeps 3.2x capacity.
Negative case 'FP8 faster only due extra expert slots' does not apply (fewer slots and inconsistent A/B), but the B difference is not robust enough to adopt.

decision.reason: no codec/residency combination beats the current nvfp4 + auto choice beyond noise; keep --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4.
decision.fp8: not adopted (no robust gain, halves capacity vs nvfp4)

cases.detail: decoded the codec effect in isolation
fp8 B edge is not residency (fewer slots, A contradicts)
KV bytes 0.24/0.40/0.77 GiB for nvfp4/fp8/bf16 at 32768 tokens

rollback_recipe: n/a (no production change; prod keeps nvfp4). Revert any experiment via drop-in.
limitations: 16k workload, single request; PPL from the 41 corpus.
A/B deltas within run noise (~3%); no repeated trials.
